role: BR-8 engineering closure. Idempotent upload and evidence-digest integrity, repaired and proven against the real product. NOT a deployment record.
productionShaReadBack: GET /health/version, three consecutive stable reads, gitCommit 32653cac2f04cab79269ad5bfeea8f4629eaf8c0, buildTimestampSourceStatus BUILD_TIMESTAMP.

defectsFound.statement: A clientRequestId replay whose first attempt had not completed drove putAndFinalize on the EXISTING row, writing the replayed bytes to the already-allocated object key while the row's sha256 continued to describe the first attempt's bytes.
defectsFound.demonstration: 01-BEFORE-DEFECT-DEMONSTRATED.txt §3. The object store was stopped so the first PUT genuinely failed, leaving the row at status 'failed' with sha256(A). Replaying the same identifier with bytes B returned HTTP 201 and left DB digest = sha256(A), live digest = sha256(B). DIVERGED.
defectsFound.materiality: The database's integrity claim about a piece of safety evidence was false. read() verifies downloads against this column, so the object became unservable — contained, but the evidence was gone.

defectsFound.statement: The idempotency lookup did not exclude retired rows, so a replayed clientRequestId naming a file the customer had DELETED wrote the bytes back to the erased object's key and flipped the row from 'deleted' to 'ready'.
defectsFound.demonstration: 01-BEFORE-DEFECT-DEMONSTRATED.txt §4. After DELETE /files/:id removed the bytes, a replay returned HTTP 201, the bytes were present in the store again, and the tombstone read 'ready'.
defectsFound.materiality: Erased customer evidence was restored to production storage through the ordinary upload route. BR-7 is CLOSED on the guarantee that erasure is final. The download route still refused the object because deletedAt remained set, so the bytes were unreachable by a customer — but they existed again, and the §312 ledger query excludes the row, so they would have become an unexplained orphan.

defectsFound.statement: The idempotency identity did not include the governed operation, so replaying an identifier while uploading to a DIFFERENT inspection returned the FIRST inspection's object.
defectsFound.demonstration: 01-BEFORE-DEFECT-DEMONSTRATED.txt §6. The second upload was answered with an object whose parentId was the first inspection.
defectsFound.materiality: The photo the caller actually sent was never stored, and the caller was handed evidence belonging to a different inspection. Contained by ownership — the row is always the caller's own — so it is a correctness defect and not a disclosure one.

defectsFound.statement: The compensating delete in putAndFinalize ran on every failure, including a failure while RESUMING a row whose bytes a previous attempt had already committed.
defectsFound.materiality: A failed replay could delete good evidence. Repaired by making the compensating delete conditional on this call having created the row.

defectsFound.state: NEW AT §314, REPORTED, NOT REPAIRED — PRODUCT-OWNER DECISION
defectsFound.statement: The §312 recovery reconciler — the SCHEDULED monitor activated at §312A — cannot detect live-byte divergence at equal length. It compares the live object's LENGTH from a bucket listing, then compares recovery-generation digests against the ROW digest; it never re-hashes the live bytes.
defectsFound.demonstration: 05-RECOVERY-INTEGRATION.txt §4, measured. With an ACTIVE object's live bytes replaced out-of-band by a payload of identical length and a different digest: reconcile-evidence-recovery reports PROTECTED and exits 0; verify-object-consistency without --deep reports CONSISTENT and exits 0; verify-object-consistency --deep exits 1; the new §314 gate exits 1.
defectsFound.correctsTheRegister: The BR-8 entry stated that verify-object-consistency.js --deep and the §312 classifier BOTH report this as DIGEST_MISMATCH. The first half is true; the second is not, for the equal-length case that BR-8 itself names.
defectsFound.residualRisk: After the §314 repair the application can no longer create this state. The residual exposure is divergence from a NON-application cause — operator error, a direct bucket write, or storage corruption — which the scheduled monitor would not raise.
defectsFound.whyNotRepairedHere: reconcile-evidence-recovery.js is §312 / BR-5 surface and BR-5 is CLOSED. Rewriting a closed blocker's monitor inside a BR-8 section would be scope expansion. It is reported with measured evidence for a product-owner decision.

theRepair.rule: A REPLAY MAY DRIVE A PUT ONLY IF THE REPLAYED BYTES ARE THE BYTES THE ROW'S DIGEST ALREADY DESCRIBES.
theRepair.why: storage_objects.sha256 is written once at row creation and never revised. Making it the WRITE AUTHORIZATION rather than a passive record closes four hazards with one rule: same-id/different-payload is refused; the loser of a concurrent race can only ever write byte-identical bytes, so last-writer-wins cannot change what is stored; the digest cannot go stale because no write that would make it stale is permitted; and a genuine resume replays the same bytes by definition and is admitted.
orderOfChecks: TERMINAL first — deleted / erasure_pending / quarantined, or any row carrying deletedAt, is refused before anything else. An identifier that named retired evidence is spent.
OPERATION — category, parentType and parentId must match the row the identifier already names.
PAYLOAD — sha256 of the replayed bytes must equal the row's recorded digest.
COMPLETED — a 'ready' row returns the committed result: no PUT, no new row, no digest change, no second audit row.
RESUME — 'uploading' or 'failed' completes using the row's OWN contentType, with bytes proven identical to the digest.

conflictSemantics.disclosure: None possible. The row is found by a predicate including createdByUserId = the caller, so a caller can only ever be told about an object they created. Another user presenting the same identifier misses the lookup entirely and creates their own row.

theRepair.digestAuthority: Computed once in store(), from the same Buffer that is handed to provider.put. Nothing between the hash and the PUT re-encodes, re-reads, streams or transforms it, so bytes-hashed and bytes-PUT are one value rather than two that must be kept in agreement. Never taken from the caller: the DTO whitelist rejects sha256, objectKey and status outright (forbidNonWhitelisted), proven in 02-AFTER-GATES.txt §10.
theRepair.schemaChange: NONE. No migration. The existing partial unique index uq_storage_object_client_request (createdByUserId, clientRequestId) already provides the concurrency containment, which is PROVEN rather than assumed in 02-AFTER-GATES.txt §7-§8. Widening it would let one identifier legitimately name several rows, which is the opposite of its purpose; the operation check is an application-layer refusal instead.

gateIsNotVacuous: Proven in both directions. Corrupting an ACTIVE object's bytes out-of-band moves the gate to INVARIANT_VIOLATED and names the object; mutating the gate to treat MISMATCHED as passing makes it report INVARIANT_HOLDS with three divergent objects present. The gate was restored byte-identically to 8b029c7921ea9ce50d66d94886dcf64511d7dd4ceef59795d2ebca10fc865a09.

productionScan.authorisation: §314 authorises a READ-ONLY scan. SELECT and GetObject only; the script has no write path.
productionScan.mode: READ_ONLY_FULL_REHASH — every object downloaded and re-hashed. Length is not integrity.
productionScan.meaning: The five real customer evidence objects verify byte-for-byte against the digests the database recorded at upload. The sixth row is the §313A production erasure proof: retired, bytes correctly absent. NO production divergence exists, so no product-owner remediation decision is required and the five customer objects were not modified.

observability.extended: storage.operation_failed now carries stage (PUT | FINALIZE) and resumable, so an upload whose bytes landed but whose finalization failed is distinguishable from one whose bytes never landed.
observability.verified: 10 replay events (7 RETURNED_COMMITTED, 3 RESUMED) and 13 conflict events covering all three reasons were emitted during the suites. Checked and found absent from every line: digests, object keys, download names, tokens. Identifiers, category, parentType and the reason code only.
observability.note: This is the §268 EMISSION layer. §268 forbids calling it monitoring, and OPS-2 remains OPEN.

apiCompatibility.unchanged: A first upload, and a replay of a completed upload with the same bytes, behave exactly as before — same 201, same body, same object.
apiCompatibility.changed: A replay that does not match the object its identifier already names now returns 409 with a reason code instead of silently returning the first object (or, worse, overwriting it). The three reasons are EVIDENCE_RETIRED, OPERATION_MISMATCH and PAYLOAD_MISMATCH.
apiCompatibility.clientImpact: The offline client mints one identifier per queued photo and replays it unchanged, which is the admitted path. A 409 means the client is asserting something different under an identifier it has already spent, which is a client defect or an attempt to substitute evidence — and in both cases surfacing it beats masking it.
